overview: This file documents an October 1940–January 1941 inquiry by the American President Lines and former senator William Gibbs McAdoo about maintaining automobile service and gasoline supplies at the company’s Kobe office under Japan’s wartime rationing regulations. Initial company reports alleged that foreign firms could no longer operate cars and that automobiles might be placed under American consular jurisdiction, but the State Department rejected that interpretation and requested a report from Kobe. Consul Samuel Sokobin subsequently explained that the company officially received eight gallons monthly plus a special allowance of 78 gallons, supplied through a United States payment arrangement with the Standard-Vacuum Oil Company, although its ration tickets were awaiting revalidation following stricter regulations effective October 1. The consular report also corrected confusion concerning the company’s Yokohama employee and the supposed precedent involving the Singer Sewing Machine Company, concluding that the Kobe office had adequate gasoline for the time being and did not yet want consular intervention.

subfiles.title: McAdoo requests assistance for the American President Lines automobile in Kobe
subfiles.from: William Gibbs McAdoo, Chairman of the Board, American President Lines
subfiles.to: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: McAdoo asks the State Department to help license an American President Lines company automobile in Kobe so that it can continue operating and obtain fuel.
subfiles.summary: McAdoo asks State to help license American President Lines' Kobe company car amid Japanese fuel restrictions.

subfiles.title: Poole reports restrictions on foreign-owned automobiles in Japan
subfiles.from: Arthur B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.about: Poole asks McAdoo to consult the State Department about placing the company’s Kobe automobile under consular jurisdiction.
subfiles.summary: Poole reports Japan barring foreign firms from operating cars or buying gasoline, citing a Singer precedent for consular jurisdiction.

subfiles.title: Long rejects proposed consular licensing arrangement
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Long replies that the State Department knows of no way to place the company automobile under the jurisdiction of the American Consulate.
subfiles.summary: Long finds no basis for consular jurisdiction over the Kobe car, calling the cited precedent a misunderstanding.

subfiles.title: Instruction to the American Ambassador in Tokyo concerning the Kobe automobile
subfiles.about: The Department transmits McAdoo’s request and its reply to the American Ambassador for information.
subfiles.summary: State forwards the Kobe car-licensing correspondence to the Tokyo Ambassador for information.

subfiles.title: Instruction to the American Consul in Kobe requesting comment
subfiles.about: The Department sends the correspondence to Kobe for the consul’s information and comment.
subfiles.summary: State forwards the Kobe car-licensing correspondence to the Consul, requesting his comment.

subfiles.title: Consular despatch on gasoline supplies for the Kobe company automobile
subfiles.from: Samuel Sokobin, American Consul at Kobe
subfiles.about: Sokobin explains the Kobe office’s gasoline allocation, ration-ticket difficulties, and reasons for declining immediate consular intervention.
subfiles.summary: Sokobin reports the Kobe firm doesn't want consular help, having secured extra gasoline informally and expecting its ration tickets revalidated.

subfiles.title: Long forwards the Kobe consular report to McAdoo
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Long sends McAdoo the American Consulate’s report on gasoline supplies for the Kobe automobile.
subfiles.summary: Long forwards Kobe's detailed report to McAdoo, answering the gasoline-licensing inquiry for the company car.

interest: Shows a 1941 American firm seeking help with Japanese gasoline restrictions on its company car in Kobe.
